channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Trump Challenges AI Guardrails
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondent Kailey Leinz discusses the calls to rein in advanced artificial intelligence models. On today's show, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Bully Pulpit International Managing Partner Adam Hodge and Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget President Maya MacGuineas. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Crypto Bill Text Released Ahead of Senate Vote
item.description: Bloomberg's Tyler Kendall broke down the potential sticking points around the Clarity Act after Senate Republicans released updated text of the bill in anticipation of a vote this week. The text includes an updated ethics provision that was a main roadblock to get Democrats on board, that would give state attorneys general some authority rules and will push elected officials to put their digital asset holdings into a blind trust or forced divestiture. The bill also faces pushback from community banks concerned about deposit flight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Dividend Would Come With 'Doozy' of a Price Tag, Says Maya MacGuineas
item.description: Maya MacGuineas, president of the Committee for a Responsible Federal Budget, on Trump’s proposal, to give $5,000 checks to adult Americans carries a `doozy' of a price tag. MacGuineas said that the president is governing with 'Oprah politics' of making fiscal promises and is concerned that both parties will fall onto a 'wagon of competing promises' to try and win over voters ahead of the midterms. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Texas Republican Slammed for Racist Post About Longhorn Fans
item.description: As Texas Longhorns football fans basked in their comeback win over top-ranked Ohio State this weekend, a photograph of gleeful students ignited a fresh round of Republican infighting over immigration and assimilation — just as the party is seeking unity ahead of the midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Joe Lovinger

item.title: House Speaker Risks Trump Ire, Signals Openness to AI Guardrails
item.description: House Speaker Mike Johnson is showing an openness to regulation of artificial intelligence that clashes with President Donald Trump’s clear hostility to the idea, creating a divide within the party just weeks before a midterm election where Republicans are already facing strong headwinds.
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson

item.title: The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations Celebrates 10 Years
item.description: For a decade, David Rubenstein has sat down with some of the biggest names in business, finance, politics and culture. We look back at 10 of the most memorable moments from "The David Rubenstein Show: Peer to Peer Conversations." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Closer Europe-Canada Ties on Trade, Defense Counter US, China: Live Q&A
item.description: Bloomberg reporters answer your questions about the close new alliance forged between the EU and Canada in a Live Q&A on Wednesday, September 16 at 9 a.m. ET.
item.dc:creator: Richard Bravo, Andrea Palasciano, Brian Platt and Oliver Crook

item.title: DOJ Covid Loan-Fraud Crackdown Finds $245 Million in Losses
item.description: The US Justice Department said a federal crackdown by prosecutors this summer uncovered hundreds of millions of dollars in fraud tied to Covid-relief programs, resulting in criminal charges against dozens of defendants.
item.dc:creator: Chris Strohm and Jimmy Jenkins

item.title: Burnham Mulls Saudi Support Amid UK Fears of Houthi Economic Hit
item.description: Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering whether to help Saudi Arabia counter attacks from the Houthis in Yemen amid UK concerns about a worsening economic hit from the escalating conflict.
item.dc:creator: Alex Wickham

item.title: Trump Jr.’s Wife Says Russian Oligarch Paid for Bahamas Parties, Not Wedding
item.description: President Donald Trump’s daughter-in-law said a Russian oligarch paid for “two incredible nights of celebration” in the Bahamas after her wedding to Donald Trump Jr. but was not involved in the actual nuptials, amid fresh ethics questions involving the first family.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron

item.title: Carney Says Canada Ready for US Trade Talks After Collapse Clarifies Red Lines
item.description: The dramatic collapse of trade talks with the US in August helped clarify Canada’s negotiating “red lines,” said Prime Minister Mark Carney, who added he’s ready to get back to the table for the right deal.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Seal and Brian Platt

item.title: Germany, UniCredit Say Commerzbank Talks Were ‘Constructive’
item.description: German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil and UniCredit SpA Chief Executive Officer Andrea Orcel said they held constructive talks Monday after the ministry outlined the demands it has for the Italian lender’s bid to take over Commerzbank AG.
item.dc:creator: Arno Schütze and Patrick Donahue

item.title: Trump Claims Russia-Ukraine Energy Truce; Kyiv Says Not Yet
item.description: President Donald Trump and Ukraine offered differing accounts of a supposed agreement with Russia to stop attacks on energy infrastructure, as strikes on oil refineries help drive diesel prices to record levels.
item.dc:creator: Hadriana Lowenkron and Jennifer A. Dlouhy

item.title: EU Draft on Social Media Limits Sees Fines of Up to 6% of Sales
item.description: The European Union is considering potential fines of as much as 6% of a company’s annual sales for online services that fail to prevent children from accessing their platforms, as part of the bloc’s plans for a social media ban for kids under the age of 15.
item.dc:creator: Gian Volpicelli and Alberto Nardelli

item.title: Carney Calls for Global AI Oversight Body to Ensure Safe Development
item.description: Canada wants to see the creation of a global “technology stability” body to help oversee artificial intelligence and ensure it is safe, Prime Minister Mark Carney said.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt and Christine Dobby

item.title: DOJ-Ticketmaster Deal Saddened Top US Lawyer Who Tried Case
item.description: The US Justice Department’s former lead litigator in the Ticketmaster monopolization case said the federal government would have won in court and gotten a better deal than the surprise settlement the Trump administration reached with the company one week into the trial.
item.dc:creator: Leah Nylen

item.title: Zelenskyy Moves to Dismiss Ukraine Chief Prosecutor in Graft Row
item.description: Volodymyr Zelenskyy took a step to dismiss Ukraine’s embattled chief prosecutor, siding with anti-corruption agencies in a showdown over a probe into an alleged call center scheme.
item.dc:creator: Olesia Safronova

item.title: Iran-Gulf Talks Delayed as Saudi Counters Houthi Attacks
item.description: A meeting between Iran and several Gulf Arab nations over a temporary shipping lane through the Strait of Hormuz was postponed, highlighting tensions with the Islamic Republic.
item.dc:creator: Salma El Wardany and Sherif Tarek

item.title: Mark Carney Seeks C$1 Trillion of Investment Amid US Trade Strains
item.description: For Mark Carney, walking away from trade talks with US President Donald Trump was politically popular. Now Canada’s leader has to contend with a more difficult economic reality.
item.dc:creator: Christine Dobby and Thomas Seal

item.title: Senator Coons Urges Congress to Act on AI Risks
item.description: Senator Chris Coons is on Bloomberg This Weekend and says Congress needs enforceable guardrails for rapidly advancing AI, warning that lawmakers are struggling to keep pace while competition with China makes a full development pause impractical. Coons also tells hosts David Gura and Christina Ruffini that managing the technology’s risks will ultimately require cooperation among industry, Congress and governments around the world. (corrects misspelling of TV host's name) (Source: Bloomberg)
